title: Notion: one shared brain for every agent
how: ffmpeg streamed the video from its URL into cutscene's measure (256 px luma, every frame); nothing saved but these numbers and stills in scratch
whyTopTier: A 36 s film that draws a system out of real screens: a terminal agent, a Notion 'Memories' page and a phone chat side by side, joined by arrows. The terminal saves a memory, the Notion page updates, and the phone's agent uses it. Each chapter opens on a claim card on warm white.
instrument: 24 fps, still 91%, 16 shots at a 2.25 s median: held frames for reading. The one clean fit (31.60, out-expo, rms 2.8%) is the logo sliding in, not a camera move.

byEye.zoom: the three surfaces at about ×0.5 each in the three-up; the terminal and the phone alone at ×1–1.5
byEye.cards: 'One shared brain for every agent', 'Save your memories and skills to Notion', 'Bring them with you to any agent'; logo
byEye.frame: warm off-white; windows with soft shadows; drawn arrows between them
byEye.sound: an audio track with rhythmic onsets (not listened to)

classify: Hand-edited feature film for a cross-tool feature. Conventions: claim cards, a multi-surface composition with connectors, typed prompts, a long logo hold.

diagnose.observation: Three real surfaces share one frame, joined by arrows.
diagnose.principle: A system diagram made of the product's own UI: juxtaposition plus connectors shows the data flow without narration.

diagnose.observation: Shots hold 2.25 s at the median; still 91%.
diagnose.principle: Reading time: terminal text needs a held frame to be read at all.

diagnose.observation: The memory saved in the terminal is the one the phone's answer uses.
diagnose.principle: Setup and payoff across surfaces: the proof is the same fact arriving elsewhere.

diagnose.observation: Terminal text is set small in the three-up.
diagnose.principle: Legibility: the composition favours the diagram over the words in it.

teaches.text: Two or three surfaces side by side for parallel action (Cursor, Family, Figma, Notion).
Draw a connector between two framed surfaces when the story is data moving between them.
Close the loop: the fact saved in one scene is used in the next.

critique.like: The arrows between three real screens draw the architecture with nothing but the product's UI.
critique.wish: The terminal is too small in the three-up to read the memory being saved; a cut to it at ×1.5 comes only later.
critique.wonder: Could a reel compose two scenes recorded separately into one frame with a connector between them?
